svg.title: The opportunity score: Opportunity equals 100 times Leverage times (0.50 Prevalence plus 0.30 Severity plus 0.20 Breadth). Prevalence is the share of the corpus, normalised to the largest theme. Severity is the share of the theme's rated items at 1 or 2 stars, falling back to model sentiment and then to the corpus detractor rate as a neutral prior. Breadth is distinct platforms carrying the theme divided by platforms in the run: a theme on all three is a category problem. Leverage, from 0 to 1, multiplies rather than adds, on purpose. A worked illustration with made up inputs, not run data: a large after delivery theme with problem size 0.90 and leverage 0.20 scores 18, while a smaller fit theme with problem size 0.40 and leverage 1.0 scores 40. Adding would let volume alone win; multiplying says a large problem with little to do with the goal is not a large opportunity for this goal. The inductive catch all is pinned to zero leverage so it can never head a ranking, and every component is a column next to the score.

div.p: Problem size is a weighted sum. The score is that size gated by leverage, so relevance to this goal decides the ranking.
Share of the corpus, normalised to the largest theme.
Share of rated items at 1 or 2★, with published fallbacks when ratings are thin.
Platforms carrying it ÷ platforms in the run. All three means a category problem.
0 to 1 per label. The inductive catch all is pinned to 0.

div.div: Worked illustration · made up inputs, not run data
div.p: Problem size: the bigger theme wins on volume.
Opportunity: the smaller, goal relevant theme ranks first. A test checks exactly this.
